description: Full auth and security truth for CreatorOS — broken Passport.js auth, target Clerk migration, API security gaps, privacy/trust/safety posture. Revised in Phase 14.6F to align with 18 ratified P0 decisions (2026-06-04).

critical_vulnerability.description: comparePasswords() returns true for ALL passwords — authentication is effectively disabled
critical_vulnerability.impact: Any password works for any user account. Zero authentication barrier. Full account takeover with only a username.
critical_vulnerability.root_cause: comparePasswords function unconditionally returns true regardless of input, bypassing bcrypt/scrypt comparison entirely
critical_vulnerability.blast_radius: All 20 database tables accessible via any authenticated session. Creator content, consumer data, products, orders, revenues, AI agent configs, community messages, documents — all exposed.
mitigating_factors: No production deployment exists — app is not publicly accessible
No real user data in database — only seed/test data
Beast and GitHub are the only live copies
critical_vulnerability.resolution_status: RESOLVED — Clerk migration ratified as first task per DEC-146B-COS-002 (2026-06-04, Phase 14.6C). Operator approved Option D: block ALL other implementation until auth complete.
critical_vulnerability.resolution_recommendation: Do NOT fix Passport.js. Migrate directly to Clerk. Fixing broken auth in a system scheduled for replacement is wasted work.
critical_vulnerability.priority: P0 — ratified. Clerk migration is the first implementation task per DEC-146B-COS-002 and DEC-146B-COS-004.

password_hashing.actual: comparePasswords returns true unconditionally — no hashing comparison occurs

registration.validation: username uniqueness enforced at DB level (unique constraint)
registration.password_policy: none — no minimum length, complexity, or strength requirements

current_auth.session_invalidation: unknown — needs audit of logout/session-destroy flow

target_auth.rationale: Clerk provides managed auth with OAuth, MFA, session management, webhook-based sync, and prebuilt React components. Eliminates need to maintain auth infrastructure. Ratified as production auth provider per DEC-146B-COS-002 (2026-06-04).
target_auth.ratification_status: OPERATOR-APPROVED per DEC-146B-COS-002. Clerk first, block ALL other implementation until auth complete.

sso.target: Enterprise tier — SAML/OIDC for creator teams and brand accounts

magic_link.rationale: Passwordless login for consumer accounts reduces friction

mfa.enforcement: required for creator accounts, optional for consumers

session_management.revocation: instant via Clerk dashboard or API

webhook_sync.target: CreatorOS backend — sync Clerk user to local users table

migration_path.recommendation: Migrate directly to Clerk. Do NOT fix Passport.js. RATIFIED per DEC-146B-COS-002.
migration_path.rationale: Fixing broken auth is wasted work when the target is a managed auth provider. Every hour spent patching Passport.js is an hour not spent on the migration that replaces it entirely. Operator ratified this approach on 2026-06-04.

phases.name: Clerk project setup
phases.description: Create Clerk application, configure OAuth providers (Google, Apple), set redirect URLs, obtain API keys

phases.name: Schema migration — users table
phases.description: Add clerk_id column to users table. Clerk becomes source of truth for identity; local users table stores app-specific fields (role, xpPoints, level, bio, profileImageUrl). Remove password column after migration.

phases.name: Backend middleware swap
phases.description: Replace Passport.js middleware with Clerk Express SDK (@clerk/express). Replace req.user population from session lookup to Clerk JWT verification. Remove express-session, connect-pg-simple, memorystore, passport, passport-local dependencies.

phases.name: Frontend auth component swap
phases.description: Replace custom login/register forms with Clerk React components (ClerkProvider, SignIn, SignUp, UserButton). Replace auth state management with useUser()/useAuth() hooks from @clerk/clerk-react.

phases.name: Webhook handler
phases.description: Implement Clerk webhook endpoint to sync user.created/updated/deleted events to local users table. Ensures local DB stays in sync with Clerk as source of truth.

phases.name: Route protection audit
phases.description: Audit all API routes in routes.ts (53KB god file) to verify every protected endpoint checks Clerk session. No route should fall through without auth.

phases.name: Session table cleanup
phases.description: Drop session table from Postgres after Clerk migration confirmed working. Remove connect-pg-simple session store configuration.

phases.name: Password column removal
phases.description: Drop password column from users table after all auth flows confirmed working through Clerk. This is a one-way door — verify thoroughly before executing.

rls.current_state: No row-level security policies exist on any of the 20 tables. All queries run with full table access once authenticated (which, given COS-AUTH-001, means always).

target.scoping_strategy: user_id or business_id scoped depending on table
tables_requiring_user_scope: posts (own posts for writes, all for reads)
products (own products for creator, all for consumer reads)
tables_requiring_business_scope: orders (business owner sees their orders, consumer sees their purchases)
channel_messages (community members for reads, own messages for writes)
target.implementation_note: Drizzle ORM does not natively support RLS. Options: (1) Neon RLS with Drizzle passthrough, (2) application-level row filtering in storage.ts, (3) Postgres policies applied via raw SQL migration. Recommend option 2 first (fastest) with option 1 as hardening layer.

rate_limiting.current: No rate limiting on any endpoint. Login, registration, API calls, file uploads — all unlimited.

target.auth_endpoints: 5 requests/minute per IP (login, register, password reset)
target.ai_endpoints: 20 requests/minute per user (AI agent interactions use OpenAI credits)

cors.current: CORS configuration not verified from code audit. Express default is no CORS headers (blocked by browsers for cross-origin requests).
cors.target: Explicit CORS whitelist for production domain only. No wildcard origins.

csrf.current: No CSRF token generation or validation observed in code audit. Express-session without CSRF protection is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery.
csrf.target: Clerk handles CSRF via its own token mechanism. If any non-Clerk auth endpoints remain, add csurf or equivalent.
csrf.note: Clerk migration may resolve this entirely — Clerk sessions use JWT tokens in Authorization header, not cookies, making traditional CSRF less relevant.

input_validation.current: Zod schemas exist for DB insert types (generated by drizzle-zod). Route-level input validation coverage is unknown — routes.ts is 53KB and needs line-by-line audit.
input_validation.target: Every API endpoint validates input with Zod before processing. No raw req.body access without schema validation.

file_upload_security.current: File upload endpoints exist (posts with imageUrl, audioUrl, videoUrl; documents; stories). Upload validation, size limits, type restrictions, and storage security need audit.
file_upload_security.target: File type whitelist, size limits (10MB images, 100MB video, 50MB audio), virus scanning for production, signed URLs for private content.

sql_injection.current: Drizzle ORM parameterizes queries by default. Risk is low unless raw SQL is used anywhere in routes.ts or storage.ts.
sql_injection.note: God file storage.ts (104KB) needs grep for raw SQL queries to confirm no injection vectors.

error_handling.current: Error handling patterns in Express routes not audited. Risk: stack traces or internal details leaking in production error responses.
error_handling.target: Global error handler that returns sanitized error messages. Never expose stack traces, DB errors, or internal paths to clients.

data_classification.current: No data classification scheme exists. User PII (username, displayName, bio, profileImageUrl), financial data (revenues, orders), and content data (posts, messages, documents) are all treated identically.

target.classification_note: Classification determines encryption requirements, retention policies, access controls, and breach notification obligations.

requirements.description: Users must be able to request and receive all data held about them
Users must be able to request deletion of all their data. Cascade deletes needed across all 20 tables where user_id appears.
Users must be able to export their data in machine-readable format
Profile editing exists. Content editing may exist. Full coverage unknown.
No cookie consent, no data processing consent, no marketing consent mechanisms
No privacy policy page or document exists
No DPA for third-party processors (Neon, OpenAI, SendGrid, Clerk)

ccpa.note: California Consumer Privacy Act applies if serving California residents. Requirements overlap significantly with GDPR.

data_retention.current: No retention policies. All data retained indefinitely.
data_retention.target: Define retention periods per data class. Deleted accounts should cascade-delete or anonymize within 30 days.

current.description: No content moderation system exists. Posts, comments, community messages, stories, and product listings have no filtering, review, or reporting mechanisms.

auto_moderation.description: Automated content screening on post/comment/message creation
layers: AI classification for nuanced content (hate speech, harassment, NSFW)
Spam detection (duplicate content, link spam, engagement farming)
auto_moderation.action_on_flag: Hold for manual review, notify creator, do not publish until cleared

manual_review.description: Human review queue for flagged content and appeals
manual_review.sla: 24 hours for flagged content review, 72 hours for appeals

appeals.flow: Content removed -> User notified with reason -> User submits appeal -> Different reviewer evaluates -> Decision is final

reporting.description: User-facing report button on all content types

requirements: identity verification (government ID or social proof)
verified + revenue threshold + content quality standards

target.rationale: Verification prevents impersonation, builds consumer trust, and gates commercial activity behind identity confirmation.

required_policies.name: Terms of Service
required_policies.description: Platform usage terms, content ownership, liability limitations

required_policies.name: Community Guidelines
required_policies.description: Acceptable behavior, content standards, enforcement consequences

required_policies.name: Creator Terms
required_policies.description: Product listing requirements, refund obligations, payout terms

required_policies.name: Acceptable Use Policy
required_policies.description: Prohibited content types, API usage limits, automation restrictions

requirements.description: Register designated DMCA agent with US Copyright Office
Endpoint/form for copyright holders to submit takedown notices
Process for accused users to dispute takedown
Policy to terminate accounts of repeat infringers

payment_fraud.note: No payment processing currently implemented. When Stripe/payment integration is added: chargeback handling, refund policies, payout fraud detection, and payment dispute resolution will all be required.

open_questions.question: What Clerk plan is needed at scale? Free tier supports 10K MAU. Pro ($25/mo) supports 100K MAU. What is the projected user count at launch and 6-month mark?
open_questions.impact: Cost planning and feature availability (SSO requires Pro, SAML requires Enterprise)

open_questions.question: Which OAuth providers beyond Google and Apple? GitHub for developer creators? Discord for gaming creators? Twitter/X for social creators?
open_questions.impact: Clerk configuration and onboarding flow design

open_questions.question: Should 2FA be required for all creator accounts or only those selling products?
open_questions.impact: Onboarding friction vs security posture. Requiring MFA for all creators is more secure but adds signup friction.

open_questions.question: Should consumer accounts use passwordless (magic link / OAuth only) while creator accounts use full Clerk auth?
open_questions.impact: Consumer UX — passwordless removes a major friction point for buyers/community members

open_questions.question: Is the current users table role model (creator/consumer) sufficient, or do we need multi-role accounts (a user who is both creator and consumer)?
open_questions.impact: Schema design — single role column vs many-to-many roles table. Current schema uses single text column with default 'creator'.

open_questions.question: What is the content moderation staffing plan? AI-first with human escalation, or human-first with AI assist?
open_questions.impact: Architecture of moderation pipeline, cost structure, response time SLAs

open_questions.question: What legal entity handles DMCA agent registration and content policy enforcement? Empyrean Studio LLC?
open_questions.impact: Legal structure needed before accepting user-generated content at scale

open_questions.question: Should RLS be implemented at the Postgres level (Neon RLS) or application level (Drizzle query filters) or both?
open_questions.impact: Defense in depth vs implementation complexity. Postgres-level RLS is harder to bypass but harder to debug. Application-level is faster to implement but relies on storage.ts always filtering correctly.

open_questions.question: What is the data residency requirement? US-only? EU option needed for GDPR?
open_questions.impact: Neon region selection, Clerk data residency, CDN configuration

implementation_debt.description: comparePasswords() returns true for all passwords — entire auth system is non-functional
implementation_debt.resolution: Replace with Clerk (do not fix Passport.js)

implementation_debt.description: No password hashing verification — stored passwords may not even be properly hashed
implementation_debt.resolution: Moot after Clerk migration — passwords will no longer be stored locally

implementation_debt.description: No email verification on registration — anyone can register with any username
implementation_debt.resolution: Clerk provides email verification out of the box

implementation_debt.description: No rate limiting on any endpoint — vulnerable to brute force and abuse
implementation_debt.resolution: Add express-rate-limit or rely on Clerk rate limiting for auth endpoints + custom middleware for API

implementation_debt.description: No RLS on any table — all data accessible to any authenticated user
implementation_debt.resolution: Implement application-level row filtering in storage.ts, then harden with Neon RLS
Clerk JWT-based auth mitigates traditional CSRF. Verify no cookie-auth endpoints remain.

implementation_debt.description: No content moderation — platform is open to abuse once public
implementation_debt.resolution: Implement auto-mod + reporting + manual review queue before public launch

implementation_debt.description: No privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) — no data export, deletion, or consent mechanisms
implementation_debt.resolution: Build data export/delete endpoints, add consent management, create privacy policy

implementation_debt.description: No content policies or terms of service — no legal framework for content disputes
implementation_debt.resolution: Draft and publish ToS, Community Guidelines, Creator Terms, AUP before public launch

implementation_debt.description: No DMCA compliance — platform liable for user-uploaded infringing content
implementation_debt.resolution: Register DMCA agent, implement takedown/counter-notice flow

implementation_debt.description: God file routes.ts (53KB) makes security audit extremely difficult — cannot verify all endpoints are protected
implementation_debt.resolution: Split routes.ts into domain-specific route modules (auth, posts, products, communities, etc.) — security auditing becomes tractable

implementation_debt.description: God file storage.ts (104KB) concentrates all data access — single point of failure for access control
implementation_debt.resolution: Split storage.ts into domain-specific storage modules with consistent authorization patterns per module

security_posture_summary.auth: BROKEN — comparePasswords bypassed, zero authentication barrier
security_posture_summary.authorization: NONE — no RLS, no row-level access control
security_posture_summary.api_security: NONE — no rate limiting, unverified CORS/CSRF
security_posture_summary.privacy: NONE — no GDPR/CCPA compliance, no data classification
security_posture_summary.content_safety: NONE — no moderation, no reporting, no policies
security_posture_summary.legal: NONE — no ToS, no DMCA, no creator verification
